title: Blueberry Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Tender, tall buttermilk pancakes folded with a double hit of blueberry — fresh berries in the batter and more scattered on top.

ingredients.name: bicarbonate of soda
ingredients.note: plus a pinch of fine salt

ingredients.name: buttermilk
ingredients.note: or 400 ml whole milk plus 1 tbsp lemon juice

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: melted, plus a knob for the pan

ingredients.name: fresh blueberries
ingredients.note: 100 g for the batter, rest to serve

steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.
Beat the eggs and buttermilk together, then stir in the melted butter.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and fold until just combined — a few lumps are fine; do not overmix.
Fold in 100 g of the blueberries.
Melt a knob of butter in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and drop in 60 ml ladles of batter.
Cook until bubbles pop on the surface, flip, then cook 1–2 minutes more until deep golden.
Keep warm on a plate under a clean tea towel while you cook the rest; serve stacked with the remaining blueberries and maple syrup.

notesMarkdown:
## Tips

- **Do not overmix.** A smooth batter means tough pancakes; stop as soon as the flour disappears.
- Keep the pan heat *medium*, not high — the outside burns before the middle sets.

> Lumps are your friend: they are pockets of lightness in the finished pancake.

## Make ahead

The dry mix keeps for a month in a sealed jar. The cooked pancakes freeze well —
cool, stack with baking paper between, and re-toast straight from frozen.

## Substitutions

- No buttermilk? Use milk soured with lemon juice (see the ingredient note).
- Frozen blueberries work without defrosting — toss them in the flour first so they don't bleed.
